title: Ignition Failure (Phoenix/Pioneer)
shortDescription: Burner did not establish flame after retries.
fullDescription:
C1 on HTP Phoenix and Pioneer combi boilers indicates ignition lockout. The unit attempts ignition three times then locks out.

Common causes are closed gas, fouled flame rod, low gas pressure, condensate-flooded burner.
safetyWarning: Gas appliance — if you smell gas evacuate and call your gas emergency line.

faq.a: Two; if returns, call a tech.

title: Flame Loss During Run
shortDescription: Flame went out during a heating cycle.
fullDescription: C2 means flame established but went out during operation. Look for flame-rod oxidation, gas pressure dips, or condensate flooding.
symptoms: Heat for short period then off

faq.a: Pull condensate trap and clean — common Phoenix issue.

title: False Flame Sense
fullDescription: C3 means the control sees a flame signal when the gas valve is closed. Treat as a gas-valve or flame-rod insulation fault.
safetyWarning: Treat as a serious safety event.

faq.a: No — fix before relying on heat.

title: High Limit Trip
fullDescription: E1 indicates the high limit opened. Common causes: air-bound HX, failed pump, closed isolation valve.
safetyWarning: Do not bypass the high limit.

title: LWCO Open
fullDescription: E2 means the LWCO has opened. Refill to spec and look for leaks.

faq.a: Rarely — repeated refills mean a leak.

title: Outlet Sensor Fault
fullDescription: E3 covers the outlet sensor on Phoenix/Pioneer. Boiler will not fire without it.

title: DHW Sensor Fault
shortDescription: Domestic hot-water sensor out of range.
fullDescription: E5 covers the DHW NTC on Phoenix and Pioneer combi units. The unit may continue heating but DHW will be unreliable.
whenToCallPro: If sensor is on a tank coil that needs draining.

title: Flue Sensor Fault
fullDescription: E6 covers the flue temperature sensor. Required for vent over-temp protection.

title: Blower / Pressure Fault
fullDescription: E9 indicates the blower is not establishing the required airflow. Usually a debris-fouled impeller, cracked APS hose, or aged blower motor.

fixSteps.title: Inspect hose
fixSteps.instruction: Check the silicone hose to APS.

faq.a: Yes — older motors are a common failure point.

title: Pump Lock Detection
fullDescription: HTP code C4 means the boiler control senses the system pump is not moving water (no flow / locked rotor). The pump may be seized, an air bubble may be trapped, or the flow switch is stuck.

fixSteps.title: Bleed Air
fixSteps.instruction: Open bleed port on pump head.

fixSteps.title: Test Pump
fixSteps.instruction: Try rotating pump shaft by hand.

whenToCallPro: If air bleeding does not free the pump, replace by a heating technician.

title: Cascade Master Lost
fullDescription: Code C5 on HTP cascade installations means the slave boiler can no longer reach the cascade master. RS-485 wiring or master power loss are common causes.

fixSteps.title: Verify Master Power
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm master boiler is on and online.

whenToCallPro: If wiring is correct and master is up, call HTP support for cascade troubleshooting.

title: Outdoor Sensor Communication Lost
shortDescription: External outdoor temp sensor not reading.
fullDescription: Code C6 means the outdoor reset sensor is open or shorted. Verify the run from boiler to outdoor sensor.
whenToCallPro: If sensor checks good, the boiler input may be faulty — call HTP support.

title: Stack Limit Open
fullDescription: Code E7 means the stack high-temperature limit opened — typically caused by a fouled heat exchanger or vent restriction.
whenToCallPro: Heat exchanger service requires a heating technician.

title: Pressure Switch Stuck
shortDescription: Air pressure switch closed before fan started.
fullDescription: Code E8 indicates the air pressure switch is showing closed at idle — switch failure or shorted wiring.

fixSteps.title: Test Switch
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect tubing; verify open at rest.

whenToCallPro: Persistent E8 after replacement is a wiring/PCB issue — call a tech.

title: Boiler Supply Sensor Short
fullDescription: Code E10: short on supply NTC. Replace sensor.
whenToCallPro: If sensor measures good, call a heating technician.

title: Boiler Supply Sensor Open
fullDescription: Code E11: open supply NTC. Reseat connector first; replace sensor if open.
whenToCallPro: If sensor checks good, call a tech for input testing.

title: Return Sensor Open
fullDescription: Code E12 is the return-side counterpart to E11.
whenToCallPro: If sensor checks good, call a tech.

title: Return Sensor Short
fullDescription: Code E13 is the short-circuit counterpart to E12.
whenToCallPro: Persistent short indicates wiring damage; call a tech.

title: Flue Sensor Fault
fullDescription: Code E14 indicates the flue thermistor is open, shorted, or out of range. The boiler uses flue temp to manage condensing operation; an invalid reading triggers lockout.
whenToCallPro: If sensor checks good, call a tech.
